To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
PRP and HA have similar anti-inflammatory and matrix restorative effects on synovial cells and chondrocells in vitro.
PRP and HA have different effects on the secretion of TNF-a by chondrocyte– synoviocyte co-cultures.

HA1PRP reduces the production of inflammatory cytokines by synoviocytes and stimulates the expression of genes involved in the production of the extracellular matrix by both synoviocytes and articular chondrocyte.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the molecular mechanisms of PRP and HA1PRP and their clinical applications.
the identification of molecular targets in the PRP that may explain its clinical effects.
the identification of PRP’s main molecular mechanisms and their clinical translation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HA and PRP have a similar effect on the secretion of selected cytokines in a 4-day co-culture model.

PRP and HA are not antiinflammatory, but rather they may have a role as anti-inflammatory and matrix restorative agents, and that the use of PRP in combination with HA should be further investigated for early management of osteoarthritis of the knee.

the combination of HA1PRP may have an effect on the secretion of TNF-a and IL-6 in synoviocytes and on the gene expression of HAS-2 and MMP-1 in synoviocytes, and on the gene expressions of COL1A1, ACAN, and MMP-13 in chondrocyte cultures, but the clinical relevance remains to be demonstrated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

PRP and HA are both effective in inhibiting the expression of TNFa, IL-1, and IL-6, but PRP is more effective than HA in inhibiting the production of MMP-13 and MMP-1 in synoviocytes, and PRP is more efficient than HA in stimulating the expression of ACAN in chondrocyte cultures.
HA1PRP may be a good candidate in early management of knee OA and that the mechanisms underlying this are not fully understood.
PRP is an interesting and safe therapeutic option, but its use is still in an experimental stage.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the anti-inflammatory and matrix restorative mechanisms of platelet-rich therapy in osteoarthritis are not well understood.
the combination of PRP and HA is synergistic and that this combination may have a role in the early management of knee OA.
PRP and HA have different mechanisms and that the combination of PRP and HA could be more effective than either alone.
